Secondly, after being in Linux, when I boot back to Windows (mainly to play games), my system clock is always off by 5 hours exactly. The time zone is still correct, but the time has shifted five hours ahead. While this is minor and trivial to fix, its kind of annoying. Does anyone have any ideas why this may be happening?

Thanks in advance!

The system clock is due to a basic incompatibility between how linux and windows do time. There's a linux setting to make it operate in a windows compatible manner though. I'll dig that out in a minute.

To get a non BIOS boot menu you'll want to set Linux as your default boot in the BIOS, then boot into Linux, open a terminal, and type this command

sudo update-grub

After that, reboot the PC, and don't bother with the BIOS menu. You should see the GRUB menu for choosing between your OSes, and windows and Linux should both be listed.

If that doesn't work, report back.
